- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (e.g., 30-day forecasts start above 75–76, while true values often exceed 78–80).
- Forecasts show upward trend bias, suggesting model assumes continued price growth rather than mean reversion or volatility.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+), model forecasts often overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly — lagging in recognizing price correction.
- Model underestimates volatility in late periods (e.g., 2023-12-07) — fails to capture sharp drops or sudden reversals.
- Forecasts tend to be smoother than true outcomes, missing short-term volatility and sudden reversals.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — forecasts rise steadily even when true values show downward corrections or volatility.
- Correction rule: reduce forecast slope after price spikes; apply mean reversion adjustment if true values deviate >10% from forecast for 2–3 consecutive days.
- If true outcome drops below 75 after a spike, reduce forecast by 2–5% per day until price stabilizes.
- Avoid linear extrapolation — use exponential decay or moving average smoothing for recent data to reduce overshoot.
- For periods with high volatility (e.g., 2023-12-07), reduce forecast confidence and apply downward bias adjustment based on recent 7-day mean.
